# Lead GWAS variants in and near peaks with driver variants

Are the peaks where phylo-FIRE attributes haplotype-selective accessibility to a
driver variant enriched for GWAS variants? The baseline throughout is all other
FIRE peaks: every consensus FIRE peak that is not a peak with a driver.

* **Peaks with a lead GWAS variant**: the percentage of peaks that contain one,
  for peaks with a driver next to all other FIRE peaks, with the observed over
  expected ratio and a Fisher exact test.
* **Distance** (`fire-figures/Rscripts/GWAS.Rmd`): for every lead GWAS variant,
  the distance to the closest peak with a driver, as a cumulative fraction,
  against same-size random samples of the other FIRE peaks.

GWAS variants are the lead (index) SNPs of associations with p < 5e-8 in the
PICS2 GWAS Catalog (2024-09-20, the release used for the FIRE paper), one row
per GRCh38 position. Overlaps are by GRCh38 position. Autosomes only. Tables come
from `scripts/hsca-gwas-tables.sh` and `scripts/hsca-driver-peaks.sh`.

```{r setup}
source("Rscripts/utils.R")
```

```{r params}
AUTOSOMES <- paste0("chr", 1:22)
N_NULL <- 10 # random samples of FIRE peaks for the distance curves
MAX_DIST <- 50e3

DRIVER <- "Peaks with a driver"
FIRE <- "All other FIRE peaks"
SET_COLORS <- setNames(c("#888888", "#d62728"), c(FIRE, DRIVER))
```

```{r load-tables}
# lead SNPs only (is_index); the table also holds every SNP linked to them
gwas <- fread("Tables/pics2-gwas-sites.tsv.gz")[
    chrom %in% AUTOSOMES & is_index == 1,
    .(chrom, start = pos - 1L, end = pos)
]

# every FIRE peak on GRCh38, with the phylo-FIRE driver call where it was tested
# (has_driver is NA for peaks phylo-FIRE did not test)
tested <- fread("metadata/hsca_driver_peaks.tsv.gz")[, .(peak_id, has_driver)]
peaks <- fread("metadata/all_peaks_hg38.tsv.gz")[chrom %in% AUTOSOMES]
peaks[, peak_id := gsub("#", "_", consensus_peak_id, fixed = TRUE)] # phylo-FIRE ids
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(peaks$peak_id))
peaks <- merge(peaks, tested, by = "peak_id", all.x = TRUE)
peaks[, is_driver := has_driver %in% TRUE]

# lead GWAS variants inside each peak
peaks <- peaks %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    bed_map(as_tibble(gwas), n_gwas = n()) %>%
    replace_na(list(n_gwas = 0)) %>%
    data.table()
peaks[, has_gwas := n_gwas > 0]

c(lead_gwas_variants = nrow(gwas))
# tested peaks, and how many of them have autosomal GRCh38 coordinates
rbind(
    tested = tested[, .(peaks = .N, with_driver = sum(has_driver))],
    on_GRCh38 = peaks[!is.na(has_driver), .(peaks = .N, with_driver = sum(has_driver))]
)
```

# Peaks with a lead GWAS variant
```{r peaks-with-gwas}
count_set <- function(x, name) x[, .(set = name, n_peaks = .N, with_gwas = sum(has_gwas))]
pct <- rbind(
    count_set(peaks[is_driver == FALSE], FIRE),
    count_set(peaks[is_driver == TRUE], DRIVER),
    # for context only, not plotted: tested peaks where no driver was found
    count_set(peaks[has_driver %in% FALSE], "HSCA-var peaks, no driver")
)[, frac := with_gwas / n_peaks]
pct[]

# Fisher exact test on peaks: peaks with a driver against all other FIRE peaks
ft <- fisher.test(table(driver = peaks$is_driver, gwas = peaks$has_gwas))
# O/E: observed share of driver peaks with a lead GWAS variant over the share
# expected from all other FIRE peaks
oe <- pct[set == DRIVER, frac] / pct[set == FIRE, frac]
test_label <- paste0(
    "O/E = ", round(oe, 2), "\np = ", format(ft$p.value, digits = 2, scientific = TRUE)
)
c(
    obs_over_exp = oe, odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate),
    ci_low = ft$conf.int[1], ci_high = ft$conf.int[2], p = ft$p.value
)
```

```{r peaks-with-gwas-plot, fig.alt="Bar chart of the percentage of peaks that contain a lead GWAS variant. Peaks with a driver are several times more likely to contain one than all other FIRE peaks, with the observed over expected ratio and the Fisher exact p-value shown above the bars."}
plot_df <- pct[set %in% c(FIRE, DRIVER)][, set := factor(set, levels = c(FIRE, DRIVER))]
bracket_y <- 1.2 * max(plot_df$frac)

plot_df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = set, y = frac, fill = set)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = percent(frac, accuracy = 0.1)), vjust = -0.4, size = 1.5) +
    # significance bracket: a line between the two bars with short tips pointing down
    geom_bracket(
        xmin = FIRE, xmax = DRIVER, y.position = bracket_y, label = test_label,
        label.size = 2, size = 0.25, tip.length = 0.03, vjust = -0.2,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = SET_COLORS) +
    scale_y_continuous(
        "Peaks with a lead GWAS variant",
        labels = percent,
        expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)) # headroom for the bracket label
    ) +
    # two rows per label
    scale_x_discrete("", labels = setNames(
        c("All other\nFIRE peaks", "Peaks with\na driver"), c(FIRE, DRIVER)
    )) +
    my_grid() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
my_ggsave("Figures/hsca-gwas-peaks-with-lead-variant.pdf", width = 1.25, height = 2)
```

# Distance from lead GWAS variants to the closest peak with a driver
```{r nearest-distance}
#' Distance (bp) from each point to the nearest interval on its chromosome:
#' 0 when the point is inside an interval, Inf when the chromosome has none.
#' Matches `bedtools closest -d`. `points` are 1 bp BED rows (position = end).
nearest_distance <- function(points, intervals) {
    iv <- as.data.table(bed_merge(as_tibble(intervals[, .(chrom, start, end)])))
    setorder(iv, chrom, start)
    out <- rep(Inf, nrow(points))
    for (chr in unique(points$chrom)) {
        v <- iv[chrom == chr]
        if (nrow(v) == 0) next
        i <- which(points$chrom == chr)
        p <- points$end[i]
        k <- findInterval(p, v$start + 1L) # last interval starting at or before p
        left <- ifelse(k > 0, pmax(p - v$end[pmax(k, 1L)], 0), Inf)
        right <- ifelse(k < nrow(v), v$start[pmin(k + 1L, nrow(v))] + 1L - p, Inf)
        out[i] <- pmin(left, right)
    }
    out
}

# self-check: inside, 1 bp past the end, between two intervals, no intervals
local({
    iv <- data.table(chrom = "chr1", start = c(100L, 200L), end = c(110L, 210L))
    pts <- data.table(chrom = c(rep("chr1", 5), "chr2"), end = c(101L, 110L, 111L, 160L, 250L, 5L))
    stopifnot(nearest_distance(pts, iv) == c(0, 0, 1, 41, 40, Inf))
})
```

```{r distance}
set.seed(1)
drivers <- peaks[is_driver == TRUE, .(chrom, start, end)]
others <- peaks[is_driver == FALSE, .(chrom, start, end)]
grid <- seq(0, MAX_DIST, by = 250)
SAMPLE <- "Random samples of all other FIRE peaks"

# cumulative fraction of GWAS variants within each distance of the closest interval
curve <- function(intervals) {
    data.table(distance = grid, fraction = ecdf(nearest_distance(gwas, intervals))(grid))
}
# each random sample has as many peaks as there are peaks with a driver
curves <- rbind(
    cbind(type = DRIVER, rep = 0L, curve(drivers)),
    cbind(type = SAMPLE, rbindlist(
        lapply(seq_len(N_NULL), function(i) curve(others[sample(.N, nrow(drivers))])),
        idcol = "rep"
    ))
)
curves[, type := factor(type, levels = c(DRIVER, SAMPLE))]
# a CDF never decreases
stopifnot(curves[, all(diff(fraction) >= 0), by = .(type, rep)]$V1)

# lead GWAS variants inside a peak (distance 0) and within 10 kb, mean over samples
dcast(
    curves[distance %in% c(0, 10e3), .(fraction = mean(fraction)), by = .(type, distance)],
    type ~ distance,
    value.var = "fraction"
)
```

```{r distance-plot, fig.alt="Line chart of the cumulative fraction of lead GWAS variants by distance to the closest peak, out to 50 kb. The curve for peaks with a driver sits above the curves for same-size random samples of all other FIRE peaks."}
TYPE_COLORS <- setNames(c(SET_COLORS[[DRIVER]], SET_COLORS[[FIRE]]), c(DRIVER, SAMPLE))
curves %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = fraction, color = type, group = paste(type, rep))) +
    geom_line(aes(linewidth = type)) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        "Distance from lead GWAS variant\nto the closest peak (bp)",
        labels = comma
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous("Cumulative fraction of lead GWAS variants") +
    scale_color_manual("", values = TYPE_COLORS) +
    scale_linewidth_manual("", values = setNames(c(0.6, 0.2), c(DRIVER, SAMPLE))) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
    theme_cowplot(font_size = 6) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
my_ggsave("Figures/hsca-gwas-distance-cumulative.pdf", width = 2.25, height = 2.5)
```

```{r distance-delta-plot, fig.alt="Line chart of the difference in cumulative fraction of lead GWAS variants between peaks with a driver and random samples of all other FIRE peaks, by distance out to 50 kb. The difference is positive at every distance."}
# Difference between two cumulative curves: peaks with a driver minus the mean
# of the random samples. This is not a CDF, so it can fall: it drops wherever
# the samples are gaining GWAS variants faster, and returns to 0 once both
# curves reach 1.
delta <- merge(
    curves[type == SAMPLE, .(null = mean(fraction)), by = distance],
    curves[type == DRIVER, .(distance, driver = fraction)],
    by = "distance"
)[, delta := driver - null]

delta %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = delta)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, color = SET_COLORS[[DRIVER]]) +
    scale_x_continuous(
        "Distance from lead GWAS variant\nto the closest peak (bp)",
        labels = comma
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous("Difference in cumulative fraction\n(peaks with a driver minus other FIRE peaks)") +
    my_grid()
my_ggsave("Figures/hsca-gwas-distance-delta.pdf", width = 2.25, height = 2.25)
```
